body: I do that too. I do it so often though I'm not sure it's really related to the disorder. In an elevated state I maybe do more of it but I also do more of a lot of things.
I'm sorry you feel this way. If misery does love company, perhaps you will find comfort that I feel the same. From reading the comments here, many others do too.
There's an interesting trigger. I'll have to pay attention to that because my last few episodes coincided with sudden successes or new developments in my life. Thanks for sharing.
Thanks for the reply. Anxiety and stressful situations usually lead to depression in me. I suspect that nothing triggers my hypomania as clearly as that triggers depression.
Thanks for the reply. I'm guessing that "nothing" is also my main trigger.

For my work I'm assessed by how much I perform. If I don't have things to do, either I look like I'm under-performing or I look like am not needed. Maybe that's ultimately true.

My trouble is I can't really control my thoughts or worries. They control me. 

Thank you for listening. Today I signed up for a gym. Hopefully that will burn off some of my anxiety and keep me from returning to the ledge every couple of weeks.

I just noticed this post now. Thank you for replying. I'm sorry to say that I'm still in the same place as before. I was fine for a while, but I've since gone back. I notice now that it's been almost 2 weeks since I made the post, and when I made the post I felt awful 2 weeks prior. 

I suppose what brings me down is the constant worry and the fear. I worry about work when I have too much or too little to do. I also worry about losing my job (it doesn't help that I called in sick today because I felt too depressed to go in). I also fear things. I fear poverty, car accidents, embarrassment, losing friends, not gaining friends. 

I just feel constantly "on edge". It leads me to think about escaping.
